newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea's trade volume falls for sixth straight yr.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea's trade volume falls for sixth straight yr.

text.p: North Korea's foreign trading volume dropped 3.7 percent to $1.98 billion in 1996, posting a sixth straight annual decline, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) said on Tuesday.
North Korea's trade deficit stood at $520 million last year, a KOTRA statement said. Exports fell 1.3 percent to $730 million from a year ago and imports dropped 5.0 percent to $1.25 billion.

The Communist state's imports of agricultural and food products jumped 48 percent to $180 million last year due to a severe food shortage, the statement said. It said some 1.05 million tonnes of food were shipped to North Korea either as imports or aid.
The Stalinist nation's exports of machinery and home appliances surged 43 percent to $82 million, thanks to a rise in processing agreements with Japan.
The agency said South Korea was the North's third largest trading partner last year. South Korea exported $69.6 milllion to the North and imported $182.4 million.
